findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-mode preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the probe reports colorScheme "normal", body background rgb(255,255,255), and text rgb(34,34,34); the dark screenshot remains light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define preference-driven surface, text, link, border, and ad-container colors.

findings.summary: Page changes are abrupt and do not preserve spatial context.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection across five MPA templates found no view-transition-name or @view-transition rule; navigation performs a full visual swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-origin cross-document View Transitions with a reduced-motion fallback, starting with the shared logo, navigation, and main content.

findings.summary: Dropdown navigation is manually positioned.
findings.evidence: Rendered source positions .rjb-drop with position:absolute; top:42px; left:0 and has no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for dropdowns while retaining the existing absolute-position fallback.

findings.summary: A third-party script requests notification permission on page load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse notification-on-start identifies notifpush.com/scripts/wpn2.js. This interrupts users before any notification-related action.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the on-load request and ask only after a clear user action that explains the benefit; remove the push vendor if notifications are not core.

findings.summary: Components rely on global media queries rather than their available container.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection shows @media(max-width:767px) rules for navigation and footer, but no @container/container-type usage across representative templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable navigation, card, results, and footer components, keeping viewport queries as fallback where needed.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not consistently visible.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found 8 of the first 30 focusable controls with neither outline nor box-shadow after programmatic focus.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible treatment to every interactive element and verify the menu and ad-adjacent controls by keyboard.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow under Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 7.6 s and Time to Interactive 10.5 s (performance 0.72), despite CLS 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the real LCP resource and delay advertising, auction, analytics, and notification code until after content is visible or user intent is known.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts block the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded two long tasks, longest 400.28 ms, with 456.39 ms total blocking time; the mobile layout observer also saw a 123 ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove low-value vendors, lazy-load ads below the fold, and split/defer remaining work so tasks stay below 50 ms.

findings.summary: The lightweight page has a large, third-party-dominated network load.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 141 requests and 2,541,549 transferred bytes; 122 requests and 2,516,086 bytes were third-party. Scripts alone transferred 1,848,603 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party performance budget, load only one consent-aware ad stack, defer noncritical resources, and cache/compress eligible resources.

findings.summary: Advertising and analytics code dominates the shipped JavaScript.
findings.evidence: HAR lists multiple overlapping ad/video stacks (MGID, Vidoomy, Aniview, DoubleClick, Clever, servg1) among the largest resources; 39 scripts transferred 1.85 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate vendors and conditionally load advertising modules only where and when an ad slot becomes viewable.

findings.summary: Third-party ad links and an iframe lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three focusable MGID ad links with no discernible name and a 1×1 advertising iframe without a title.
findings.suggestedFix: Require accessible ad markup from vendors, label actionable ad links, and mark tracking iframes presentational or give meaningful titles.

findings.summary: Inline links are distinguishable only by low-contrast color.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 1.77:1 contrast between #0033cc links and surrounding #222 text and found no non-color cue for three representative links.
findings.suggestedFix: Underline inline links and choose colors with at least 3:1 contrast against surrounding text and 4.5:1 against the background where required.

findings.summary: The document landmark and heading hierarchy are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark and an H1-to-H5 heading jump for “Navegue pelo site”; representative probes likewise found no MAIN element.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in <main> and use sequential headings based on document structure, not visual size.

findings.summary: The page triggers a permission prompt on load and logs browser inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed notification-on-start and inspector-issues; the latter contains extensive cookie-policy issues from ad vendors.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove on-load permission requests and resolve vendor cookie/deprecation issues before enabling those integrations.

findings.summary: Cookies and CSP do not provide a strong secure default.
findings.evidence: Cookie audit found four cookies flagged, including three without Secure and two 400-day analytics cookies. CSP only upgrades/blocks mixed content and does not restrict script sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all cookies Secure with appropriate SameSite, shorten analytics retention, and deploy a restrictive nonce/hash-based CSP.

findings.summary: The tracking and advertising footprint is disproportionate to the content.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 31 third-party origins and known Google tracking domains; HAR attributes 2.52 MB and 122 requests to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and remove nonessential vendors, gate optional analytics/ads on valid consent, and minimize identifiers, retention, and event volume.

findings.summary: Notification permission is requested out of context.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse traces an on-load notification request to notifpush.com before the user expresses intent; no relevant notification control appears in the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Request notification permission only after an explicit, informed opt-in action.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no X-Content-Type-Options, no X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, and no Permissions-Policy. The CSP has no source restrictions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, frame-ancestors, a minimal Permissions-Policy, and a restrictive CSP; retain HSTS and Referrer-Policy.

findings.summary: The unsolicited notification prompt is a nagging consent pattern.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse confirms notification permission is requested automatically on page load, before context or a user gesture.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace automatic prompting with an honest, dismissible explanation and explicit opt-in, or remove push notifications.

findings.summary: The logo has no responsive source and uses a legacy raster format.
findings.evidence: Images evidence reports the sole authored image as PNG with no srcset; it is displayed at 295 px from a 480 px source.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide AVIF/WebP responsive sources with an appropriate srcset while retaining the existing dimensions and fallback.

findings.summary: The page performs substantial non-content background work.
findings.evidence: HAR records 46 XHR/fetch requests plus overlapping ad auctions, analytics, push, and video scripts; trace blocking time is 456.39 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate redundant background vendors and defer optional fetches until idle, visibility, consent, or explicit interaction.

findings.summary: Third-party and media cost is not proportionate to this text-first portal.
findings.evidence: Of 2.54 MB transferred, 2.52 MB was third-party; the authored page has one small image, while ad/video stacks account for most bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a strict third-party byte/request budget, avoid autoplay video, and lazy-load one vetted monetization stack per visible slot.

taskList.title: Remove or consent-gate redundant ad, tracking, video, and push vendors
Harden CSP, cookie attributes, and browser security policies
Repair landmarks, headings, ad names, iframe semantics, link contrast, and focus visibility
Modernize responsive navigation with container queries, anchored dropdowns, and transitions
Serve the logo with responsive modern image sources
